attempts.rationale: Weighted by inverse error on full pool

The series has strong trend and seasonality but moderate ranking stability; a robust non‑weighted approach like median may reduce influence of outlier model errors and capture consensus across correlated groups.
test a simple mean of the full pool to see if averaging beats median given strong trend and seasonality.
Trim extremes to mitigate correlated error groups
test a different kind of strategy – a DBA weighted average over the full pool, as the diagnosis hints weighted but we haven't tried DBA yet.
test a weighted combination on the reduced, low‑error pool (pool4) using inverse_error weights to see if focusing on the top models improves over median/trimmed_mean.
softmax weighting on the diversified pool4
The series has strong trend and seasonality; the weighted pools with inverse_error and softmax performed close to median. A simple mean over the diversified pool4 may yield a competitive score.
Test a per‑horizon weighted combination using the top‑k mean per horizon from pool4 (captures horizon‑specific strengths).
I want to see if trimming outliers from the diversified pool4 improves the weighted mean, as hinted by the high correlation groups.
Test a weighted combination on the full pool using the inverse-error handle w1 to see if a more aggressive weighting improves over trimmed_mean.

decision.justification: Selected 'trimmed_mean on pool4' (an agent proposal) as the best of 12 backtested attempts, score 0.9049. Series context: trend strength 0.9096 and seasonal strength 0.7919; model ranking is moderate across windows (Kendall tau 0.306); 3 of 19 models carry independent error; relative error spread across the pool is 3.153.
